title: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and MOGAD

steps.tx: **Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder** is an aggressive autoimmune **astrocytopathy** mediated by pathogenic immunoglobulin G autoantibodies directed against **aquaporin-4** water channels concentrated on astrocyte foot processes. Binding of autoantibodies activates the classic complement cascade, producing astrocytic lysis, secondary oligodendrocyte destruction, and severe demyelinating necrosis.

steps.tx: Longitudinally extensive **transverse myelitis** is defined on spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging by continuous T2 hyperintensity spanning **3** or more **contiguous vertebral** body segments, characteristic of **NMOSD**. These expansive lesions typically occupy central cord grey matter with marked swelling and central cord necrosis.

These expansive lesions typically occupy central cord grey matter with marked swelling and central cord necrosis.

left.title: NMOSD Myelitis (LETM)
points: Severe complete paraplegia and sphincter loss
Frequent cord swelling and central necrosis

right.title: Multiple Sclerosis Myelitis
points: Peripherally located in posterior or lateral columns
Mild to moderate sensory or motor impairment

steps.tx: **Area postrema** syndrome is a core clinical manifestation of **NMOSD**, producing **intractable hiccups**, nausea, and vomiting due to periventricular medullary inflammation in the dorsal brainstem. The area postrema lacks a tight blood-brain barrier, allowing circulating aquaporin-4 antibodies direct access to astrocytic targets within the emetic reflex centre.

The area postrema lacks a tight blood-brain barrier allowing circulating aquaporin-4 antibodies direct access to astrocytic targets within the emetic reflex centre.

left.title: Clinical Hallmarks
points: Incessant hiccups lasting days to weeks

right.title: Neuroanatomical Substrate
points: Dorsal medulla oblongata at fourth ventricular floor
Dense concentration of aquaporin-4 water channels
High sensitivity to complement-mediated astrocytic lysis

steps.tx: Targeted maintenance therapies approved for AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD include the complement C5 inhibitors **eculizumab** and ravulizumab, the interleukin-6 receptor antagonist **satralizumab**, and the CD19-directed monoclonal antibody inebilizumab. These specialized monoclonal antibodies dramatically suppress clinical relapse rates and mitigate cumulative permanent disability.

rows: Broad depletion of B-cells and plasmablasts

steps.tx: Standard multiple sclerosis disease-modifying agents such as **interferon-beta**, natalizumab, and fingolimod may exacerbate or trigger catastrophic relapses in **NMOSD** and are strictly contraindicated. Inappropriate administration of these multiple sclerosis therapies drives massive astrocytic inflammatory cascades and severe neurological worsening across the neuraxis.

steps.tx: Myelin **oligodendrocyte glycoprotein** antibody-associated disease (**MOGAD**) is an oligodendrogliopathy presenting with bilateral optic neuritis with marked optic disc swelling, LETM, or acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. Unlike NMOSD astrocytopathy, MOGAD causes primary inflammatory demyelination with relative preservation of underlying axons in clinical diagnostic evaluations.

Unlike NMOSD astrocytopathy MOGAD causes primary inflammatory demyelination with relative preservation of underlying axons.

left.title: MOGAD Features
points: ADEM presentation prominent in young children
Frequent longitudinally extensive optic neuritis with disc edema

right.title: NMOSD Features
points: Area postrema and brainstem syndromes prominent
Severe cumulative disability after acute attacks

steps.tx: Optic neuritis in MOGAD typically shows longitudinally extensive retrobulbar optic nerve and perineural **optic sheath** enhancement with sparing of the **optic chiasm**, distinguishing it from AQP4-NMOSD. Patients frequently develop prominent bilateral optic disc edema that improves rapidly with systemic high-dose pulse corticosteroids.

left.title: MOGAD Optic Neuritis
points: Marked optic nerve head swelling and disc edema

right.title: AQP4-NMOSD Optic Neuritis
points: Frequent posterior optic tract and chiasm lesions
Absence of marked anterior sheath enhancement
High risk of permanent complete visual loss

steps.tx: Acute disseminated **encephalomyelitis** presents in children with **post-infectious** encephalopathy and widespread multifocal, poorly marginated demyelinating white matter lesions on MRI, frequently associated with transient MOG-IgG positivity. Most pediatric patients achieve complete functional recovery following high-dose pulse corticosteroid therapy in specialized paediatric centres.
